outputs.explanation: Scatter plot where each marker represents an individual sample (n=141 samples plotted individually); marginal histograms also show binned individual data.

Plot shows mean ± s.d. per reporter/cell line as points with error bars; each plotted symbol already represents one cell-line/reporter combination (not an aggregate needing overlay of raw replicates), and with 6 replicates per point overlaying would clutter a log-scale multi-group scatter. Error bars are defined, satisfying variability reporting without individual overlay requirement typical for scatter-style summary plots.
These are density/line curves (kernel density-like distributions), a line plot type which is exempt from requiring individual data point overlay.
Box plots have individual data points (dots) overlaid on top of the boxes for each cell line, showing the underlying ridge-length measurements.
Polar histograms are a histogram/distribution type; individual data points are not required to be overlaid on such aggregated distribution plots.
Polar histogram averaged by subtype; distribution-type plot exempt from individual point overlay requirement.
Line plot illustrating a single example fit (original data trace, fitted function, decay envelope); this is an illustrative line plot, not an averaged summary requiring individual points.
Scatter plot where each marker represents an individual sample (n=117 samples), with error bars reflecting fit uncertainty; individual data points are inherently shown as the plotted markers.
